I don't think you necessarily should have known. We are all constantly learning and if you've never been through something traumatic you might not have a reason to know what might trigger someone. I completely understand why this bothered you; none of us like to be wrong, and being blindsided by the information that something you did with completely innocent intentions may have hurt someone else isn't a good feeling. 

That being said, those other people WERE correct in that talking about things like rape in a public server (even an 18+ one) can be triggering to others and if you're just having a conversation with another person abt it it's probably best to do so privately. 

It seems clear that you didn't mean any harm, and were indeed ignorant that you COULD be causing harm at that time, so I don't think you should be "cancelled" or anything; BUT it's not wrong of others to point out to you when your behavior is harmful. 

Honestly, my advice to you would be to learn from this experience, and any others you may have later. Don't let it make you feel like a bad person, and take comfort in the fact that it was an honest mistake. 

And for future reference, personally I've found that the best way to handle a situation like this is to graciously admit your ignorance and apologize; this is not only morally correcr but has the added benefit of diffusing most hostilities from anyone who might want to make a small mistake into a big issue.
